title: Actual quotient-augmentation reflector over completed coefficient sheaves
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R$ and a uniformizer $t$, and put $A_n=R/t^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Assume $(R,(t))$ satisfies [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. On the small pro-etale site of a scheme $T$ put $B_T=\varprojlim_n(A_n)_T$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], and use the ordinary unbounded derived category $D(B_T)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For $H\in D(B_T)$ write $Q_T(H)_n=\operatorname{Res}_n(H\otimes^L_{B_T}(A_n)_T)$ for the strict quotient tower on a single flat-term K-flat representative, with transitions induced by $A_{n+1}\to A_n$ and augmentation $x\mapsto x\otimes1$ [def-weil-integral-reduction-tower, def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules, lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Put $C_T(H)=R\lim Q_T(H)$, using total right derived inverse limit on strict towers, and let $\eta_{T,H}:H\to C_T(H)$ be the map induced by this augmentation [lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit].
Let $\Lambda_T(H)$ be the intrinsic Koszul completion of [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion], with its specified unit $\kappa_H$; that definition is formed over its own presentation $\varprojlim_n(R^\uparrow/(t)^n)_T$ of the coefficient sheaf, and $H$, $\Lambda_T(H)$ and $\kappa_H$ are transported between it and $B_T$ by restriction along the canonical ring-sheaf isomorphism $e_T$ of [lem-weil-pbc-integral-coefficient-presentation-comparison]. There is a natural isomorphism $a_H:\Lambda_T(H)\xrightarrow{\sim}C_T(H)$ identifying the actual units, $a_H\kappa_H=\eta_{T,H}$, under the normalized strict Roos comparison. The object $C_T(H)$ is locally derived $tB_T$-complete, meaning that on every slice $U$ and every $b\in tB_T(U)$ its derived internal Hom from $B_{T,U}[1/b]$ vanishes [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. For every such locally complete $L$, precomposition with the actual $\eta_{T,H}$ is a bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}(C_T(H),L)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}(H,L),\quad f\longmapsto f\eta_{T,H}.$$
Under $a_H$, this map agrees with the Koszul reflector Hom bijection $g\mapsto g\kappa_H$. Local derived completeness, intrinsic completeness (invertibility of the specified $\kappa_H$), the Roos-triangle predicate [def-weil-derived-complete], and invertibility of this actual $\eta_{T,H}$ are equivalent. These are assertions about all unbounded $H$, not just objects already complete.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sp-completed-coefficient-regular-quotients] with $O=R$, $\pi=t$ and the given scheme $T$. Its coefficient ring $\mathcal O_{E,T}$ is identified with $B_T=\lim_n(R/t^n)_T$ by the canonical isomorphism of [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers], which commutes with the projections to the constant quotients $(A_j)_T$ and with the constant scalar $t$; all assertions below are transported along this ring-sheaf isomorphism. Thus multiplication by $t$ is injective on $B_T$, and the actual projections identify $B_T/t^nB_T$ with $(A_n)_T$, compatibly with every quotient transition. These are statements about sheaf quotients, so no surjectivity on arbitrary section rings is being assumed. Countable products of $B_T$-module sheaves are exact by [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact]. These hypotheses hold for every scheme $T$.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-coefficient-presentation-comparison] the ring-sheaf isomorphism $e_T$ from the coefficient sheaf of [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion] to $B_T$ commutes with all projections to the finite quotients, hence sends the residue-defined action of $t$ to $t$; restriction along $e_T$ is an isomorphism of module categories, so it carries Koszul complexes, termwise tensor products, countable products and the signed fiber to the same constructions over $B_T$. Use the same flat-term K-flat representative $P$ of $H$ to read [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion] through $e_T$. For the one-element generating list $(t)$ its finite complexes are $K_n=[B_T\xrightarrow{t^n}B_T]$ with transition $(t,1)$. Its specified completion is the signed product fiber of $V_\bullet=(P\otimes K_n)_n$, and its unit has coordinates $((p\otimes1)_n,0)$. By exactness from Step 1, [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison] identifies this fiber with $D_T(H)=R\lim V_\bullet$; its normalization sends that zero-second-coordinate map to the map $k_H:H\to D_T(H)$ induced by the strict degree-zero augmentation. Write $b_H:\Lambda_T(H)\xrightarrow{\sim}D_T(H)$ for this comparison. Thus $b_H\kappa_H=k_H$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-regular-roos-koszul-unit] over $\mathcal O=B_T$ with regular global section $t$ (Step 1), passing to a site small in the module universe as in its hypotheses. The identifications $B_T/t^nB_T\cong(A_n)_T$ identify its strict quotient tower with $Q_T(H)$, including the augmentations. It gives $c_H:D_T(H)\xrightarrow{\sim}C_T(H)$ with $c_Hk_H=\eta_{T,H}$. Explicitly its strict tower map is $1_P\otimes\epsilon_n$, where $\epsilon_n:K_n\to(A_n)_T[0]$ is the residue projection in degree zero and zero in degree $-1$. It commutes with transitions since quotient after multiplication by $t$ in degree $-1$ is zero and the degree-zero transition is the quotient map. It sends $p\otimes1$ to $p\otimes\overline1$. Set $a_H=c_Hb_H$; the two unit equations give $a_H\kappa_H=\eta_{T,H}$. Both the strict quotient comparison and normalized Roos comparison are natural, so $a_H$ is natural.

source.place: Tags 099B, lemma-derived-completion, and 0A0E, lemma-derived-completion-koszul; regular-generator actual-unit comparison.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-koszul-completion-reflector] to $(B_T,(t))$. Its tower is exactly $V_\bullet$ and its specified unit is $k_H$. It asserts that $D_T(H)$ is locally derived $tB_T$-complete on every slice, for every local section of that ideal, and that $g\mapsto gk_H$ is bijective into any locally complete $L$. The isomorphism $c_H$ makes $C_T(H)$ locally complete as well: after slice restriction and derived internal Hom an isomorphism still has zero target precisely when its source is zero. Since $b_H\kappa_H=k_H$ (Step 2), $g\mapsto g\kappa_H$ on $\operatorname{Hom}(\Lambda_T(H),L)$ is the composite of the bijection $g\mapsto gb_H^{-1}$ with $g'\mapsto g'k_H$, hence bijective. For such $L$, the isomorphism $a_H$ gives a bijection $f\mapsto fa_H$ from $\operatorname{Hom}(C_T(H),L)$ to $\operatorname{Hom}(\Lambda_T(H),L)$. For every $f$ its image under the Koszul Hom map is $(fa_H)\kappa_H=f\eta_{T,H}$. The bijection is therefore exactly precomposition with the actual quotient augmentation, and the asserted agreement of Hom maps follows.

proof.text: The equivalences (i)--(iv) in [lem-sf-regular-roos-koszul-unit], specialized as in Step 3, identify local derived $tB_T$-completeness, invertibility of $k_H$, the existence of a quotient Roos triangle with the actual reduction components, and invertibility of $\eta_{T,H}$. Since $b_H$ is invertible and $b_H\kappa_H=k_H$, invertibility of $k_H$ is equivalent to intrinsic completeness. By [def-weil-derived-complete] its predicate is precisely existence of that quotient Roos triangle; the transition-normalized quotient identifications of Step 1 preserve both the $1-s$ arrow and the actual reduction components. This uses the regular-generator theorem to deduce invertibility of the actual unit from the existential triangle; it does not identify an arbitrary triangle isomorphism with that unit. None of these applications assumes that $H$ is complete or bounded.
